summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis and a history of autonomic dysfunction, esophagitis, and neurocognitive disorder was admitted after returning to the hospital following an ER visit for epigastric pain and dysuria. She was concerned about inadequate hepatology evaluation. During admission, her epigastric pain, which radiated to the left shoulder and worsened with eating, was managed as esophagitis with omeprazole. Urine cultures showed mixed flora consistent with contamination, and ciprofloxacin was discontinued. Orthostatic hypotension was confirmed, and her chronic pain, anxiety, and cognitive issues were monitored. She improved clinically, remained stable, and was discharged after two days with follow-up plans in primary care, hepatology, neurology, and psychiatry.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver with ascites
Disorder of the autonomic nervous system, unspecified
Dementia in other diseases classified elsewhere, unspecified severity, without behavioral disturbance, psychotic disturbance, mood disturbance, and anxiety
